title: rapid TTFT stabilizer and customer bridge for regional short-session sag
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Several enterprise customers reported sudden regressions in Time-To-First-Token (TTFT) and tokens/sec on short interactive sessions across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. This ticket coordinates an urgent triage, an emergency mitigation that can be rolled to production, and a customer-facing bridge until a permanent fix lands.
reproduction_steps: 1) Send 1-3 request fanout priming requests with short prompt (<40 tokens) to models with long context windows.
2) Observe initial token emission delay on first request after worker warmup or after router rebalancing (~300-800ms extra).
3) Confirm tokens/sec drop on sustained short sessions compared to baseline metrics in the perf dashboard.
investigation_summary: Initial telemetry shows TTFT spikes correlate with increased async KV serialization latency introduced by recent scheduler refactor (commit: abcd1234).

Root contributors: (a) the async serializer adds per-request tail work that blocks one-hot worker threads during short sessions, (b) a new batching heuristic increased batch wait timeout for low-concurrency routes, (c) regional routing changes funneling more short sessions to a small set of workers causing contention.
Impacted environments: Hosted (all regions), Dedicated clusters with >50% short-session traffic, Private (customer A, customer C) where routing affinity is enabled.
Observed variance across models: lightweight 2B/4B models show the largest TTFT delta; larger models see smaller proportional change but tokens/sec still affected under high parallelism.
temporary_mitigation_plan: 1) Deploy emergency config override to disable async KV serialization for short sessions (<128 tokens) on canary in us-west-2 (rollout target: 3% -> 25% -> 100%),
2) Reduce batching wait-time heuristic from 30ms->10ms for low-latency routes for the same canary,
3) Add router steering rule to distribute short-session traffic more evenly across worker pools for impacted regions,
4) Open customer-bridge with top 5 impacted accounts and provide traffic-routing opt-out and SLA credits as appropriate.
permanent_work_items: A) Refactor async serializer to use background worker pool that cannot block inference threads (design doc link in links),
B) Update batching heuristic to consider short-session signals and real-time latency SLO feedback,
C) Add per-tenant circuit-breaker that detects serialization backlog and falls back to sync-safe path,
D) Improve observability: add per-request KV serialization time and per-worker backlog gauges to console dashboards.
rollout_steps: Canary 03/12: emergency config applied to canary in us-west-2 (3% traffic).
Canary 03/13: expanded to 25% after 90m with TTFT reduction observed (-230ms median for short sessions).
Regional 03/14: expanded to all us-west and us-east regions while locking Dedicated pools to safe config. Monitoring active.
Full 03/16: target full rollout after validation and customer confirmations.
postmortem_notes: Immediate cause: scheduler refactor changed interaction between batching heuristic and async serializer; edge-case path created head-of-line blocking for short sessions.
Why it escaped testing: e2e perf tests used long-running synthetic sessions that masked short-session serialization latency; no regression test for small-primed fanout pattern.

Action items: add short-session synthetic scenarios to perf CI, require perf sign-off for scheduler-related refactors, and add an alert when median TTFT for short sessions increases >100ms over baseline.
